Give your decisions a rulebook.

Start with one condition, define its decision, and make the fallback explicit.

AI provides evidence. Your rules decide what happens.

Conditions are evaluated in order. The first matching branch wins. Missing or incompatible input is an error—not an automatic Else.

Re-evaluate after every return.

Use exactly one condition branch. Connect its output to the loop body, and connect the body back to this rule. Else exits; reaching the iteration limit stops for review.

RULE CONTRACT

Always return a decision.

{ "decision": {
  "type": "process",
  "code": "prepare_task",
  "processId": "…"
} }

A process decision names a contract. Connect its branch output to a process node with that same definition. No process is invoked behind the graph.

Use the right Jev value.

choice is a category key. score and confidence are numbers. noul is P(yes), not confidence.

Literal strings need JSON quotes: "project". A number is 0.85, not "0.85".

Define a process once. Reuse it in your flows.

Name its purpose, declare its inputs and outputs, and map the values it returns.

A clear contract between steps.

A process takes typed input and produces typed output. Its output can become another prompt's workflow_input, a rule's evidence, or an event payload.

Contract only. No external action will run.

The simulator validates inputs, records the requested process, emits review events, and stops. Native adapters and explicit approval are required for real execution.

WORKSPACE EVENT CATALOG {{logicCatalog.length}}

Publishers and their explicit subscribers. Identically named events from different nodes do not automatically share listeners.

Visible causality.

Every emitted envelope has an ID, source, sequence, correlation ID, and cause. Inspect actual payloads in the flow trace.

Control transitions schedule first; event listeners are queued in connection order. End or Review cancels remaining queued work. Global step and event limits prevent runaway chains.
